description: COMPOSE IS A SINGLE LANE AGAINST A GROWING POOL — A CAPACITY CONSTRAINT, NOT A LOSS. MEASURED 2026-09-05 over the most recent 20,000 gap-drain events: 326 distinct gap ids appear, 570 events are a dispatch or a successful compose nudge, and the picker reports a pool of 236 gaps with 59 excluded as hopeless. Individual gaps recur 1,115 to 1,117 times in that window, so nothing is being discarded — the same items are re-offered continuously and the picker selects the highest-scoring one each time. THE REAL CONSTRAINT: feature_compose refuses a DIRECTED compose at 2 in flight and an AUTONOMOUS one at 1, so effectively one authoring attempt proceeds at a time. Against a pool of this size that sets a hard ceiling on how fast filed work can be attempted, independent of how good the authoring is. Measured in this session from the operator side: eleven directed dispatches produced two correct landings, several correct refusals, and repeated BUSY responses — and the system's own message for BUSY is explicit that it is 'a transient capacity condition, not a capability gap'. WHY THIS IS WORTH TRACKING SEPARATELY from authoring quality: a reachability gate, better goals, or a stronger drafter all raise the value per attempt, but none raises the number of attempts. If the intent is for the substrate to work a backlog of this size autonomously, concurrency is the lever, and it is currently one. FALSIFIER: closed only when the effective concurrent-compose limit is raised and the change is demonstrated — cite the new limit and a drain-log window showing two composes proceeding simultaneously — or a measurement is cited showing per-gap latency falling with the limit unchanged. A closure citing skip-rate percentages is fabricated, because skips are backpressure and not loss.
